newsitem.title: GERMANY: German wheat broadly steady in quiet market.
newsitem.headline: German wheat broadly steady in quiet market.

text.p: German wheat prices are holding broadly steady in a quiet market, with sellers concentrating on completing previous business, brokers said on Tuesday.

Prices over the next few weeks were seen underpinned by interest from the southern European milling industry in high quality grades and by European consumer demand ahead of the 1997 harvest amid thinning supplies.
Feed wheat and barley prices benefited from export demand and a high rate of use in domestic compound feed mixes, where prices of imported protein and starch feeds remained high.
The Hamburg grain exchange this week left its spot bread wheat price (12.5 percent, 220 Hagberg) at 280 marks a tonne free Hamburg and also kept the spot feed wheat price unchanged at 275.
Fob Baltic sellers quoted first half April delivery 12 percent protein wheat steadier at 282.50-295 marks.
First half April material with 13/14 percent protein was in a broadly unchanged 287.50-309 marks range.
Fob Baltic barley was steadier at 262.50-285 marks, depending on shipment sizes.
Fob rye sellers were also a touch higher at 262.50-275 marks.
